title: Imaging Analysis Protocol for Multi-Signal Neuron Morphology
author: Nanda, Bhattacharjee, et al.
materials: Drosophila larva w1118, UAS-GMA::GFP; GAL4[477], UAS-mCherry::Jupiter
Drosophila larva w1118, UAS-GMA::GFP; +; GAL4[221], UAS-mCherry::Jupiter
Timing: [Minutes for a single simulation run]

steps.title: Install required software and dataset
steps.instruction: Download the example dataset from https://doi.org/10.17632/wpzd2wxtgn.1 (contains eight folders). Install FIJI (download zip from imagej.net/Fiji and run the installer). Install Vaa3D version 3.1 from https://github.com/Vaa3D/release/releases/tag/v3.100 and run the installer. Install neuTube from neutracing.com/download. Install MATLAB (tested with R2018a).

steps.title: Add multi‑channel plugin to Vaa3D
steps.instruction: Create a folder named multi_channel_swc under Vaa3D-3.100/bin/plugins. Copy the compiled library (.dll for Windows or .dylib for mac) from the dataset folder Vaa3D_MultiChannel_Compiled_Library into the newly created multi_channel_swc folder.

steps.title: Update TREES toolbox start script
steps.instruction: In the dataset’s Repair subfolder, edit tre_start.m so that the path at the top points to the correct TREES Toolbox subfolder under the main dataset. Copy the edited tre_start.m to all relevant subfolders inside the Quantify folder.

steps.title: Prepare scaled SWC files for quantification
steps.instruction: Open MATLAB, navigate to the Quantify/Basic_Quantification subfolder, and copy all scaled .swc files of the neuron type you wish to analyse into this folder.

steps.title: Run 20‑column cytoskeletal quantification script
steps.instruction: Execute Cyto_Ana_Regular_20Col.m in MATLAB. The script iterates over every neuron in the folder and calculates 20 values per compartment (e.g., topological distance, microtubule quantity, F‑actin quantity, diameter, branch order, etc.). At the bottom of the script change the output file name to match the neuron type (e.g., for Class IV Form3‑OE rename from C4_20Column.mat to C4Form3OE_20Column.mat).

steps.title: Compute topological distributions with TopologicalAna
steps.instruction: Run TopologicalAna.m which creates RealToPo.mat containing Strahler‑order and path‑distance distributions of length, microtubule and F‑actin. Rename the file to reflect the neuron type (e.g., RealToPo_C4WT.mat for Class IV wild‑type).

steps.title: Process each neuron type sequentially
steps.instruction: Remove the current .swc files from Basic_Quantification, copy the scaled .swc files of the next neuron type, and repeat steps 4 through 6 for all neuron groups (Class IV WT, Class I WT, Class IV Form3‑OE).

steps.title: Generate Sholl‑like plots from RealToPo
steps.instruction: Copy all RealToPo.mat files (one per neuron type) into the PD_Strahler_Based_Quant folder. The provided script processes three specific types; edit the script if additional types are needed.

steps.title: Normalize cytoskeletal quantities
steps.instruction: Run norm_script.m which normalizes each compartment’s microtubule and F‑actin quantities to the average total microtubule and average total F‑actin of Class IV WT neurons. Rename any .mat file references inside the script to match your data set.

steps.title: Create Strahler and path‑distance figures
steps.instruction: Execute TopoAna_Graph.m to produce figures of length, microtubule and F‑actin versus Strahler order and path distance. The script is preset for three neuron types; modify it for other groups as required.

steps.title: Correlate arbor length with parameters
steps.instruction: Copy C4_20Column.mat (for Class IV) into the ArborLength_Corr folder and run Arbor_Len_Corr.m. The script computes Pearson (linear) correlations between local arbor length and each of the following: path distance, branch order, diameter, local microtubule quantity, and local F‑actin quantity.

steps.title: Measure local F‑actin change distribution
steps.instruction: Duplicate the Quantify folder to Quantify_actin_enrichment. Run Fdelta_CurveShifts.m which calculates the relative local F‑actin change (FΔ = (Fc‑Fp)/Fp) for each compartment and generates cumulative frequency distribution curves for bifurcating, elongating, and terminating compartments. Use the appropriate C4_20Column.mat (or equivalent) for each neuron group.

steps.title: Launch dendritic growth simulations
steps.instruction: In the Simulation folder, locate the subfolders for the three neuron types. Inside each subfolder run Auto_M_F_Sim_MHSorted.m . The script creates .mat files describing simulated neurons and stores them in the same subfolder’s Simfolder directory.

steps.title: Convert simulated data to SWC files
steps.instruction: Within the analysis subfolder run createSwCsMultiNeuBW.m . This script reads each simulated .mat file and outputs two SWC files per neuron: one where the diameter column encodes microtubule quantity and one where it encodes F‑actin quantity.

steps.title: Quantify simulated neuron properties
steps.instruction: Copy the generated simulated SWC files into Quantify/Sim_Neuron_Basic_Quantification (replacing any existing SWCs). Run SimNeuronsProperties.m to compute the same 20 compartment properties (except three that are not applicable) as for real neurons.

steps.title: Analyze simulated topological distributions
steps.instruction: Run TopologicalAna_Sim.m to obtain Strahler‑order and path‑distance distributions of length, microtubule and F‑actin for the simulated neurons.

steps.title: Compile real and simulated results for comparison
steps.instruction: Move the three real‑neuron RealToPo.mat files and the three simulated‑neuron output files into Quantify/Comparative_Analysis_of_real_and_Simulated_Neurons. Then run Comparative_Topological_Cytoskeletal_Dist.m which plots simulated distributions as thin dark lines over the real distributions shown as thicker lighter lines.

description: Techniques for digitally reconstructing neuron morphology from light microscopy are aplenty (Acciai et al., 2016; Peng et al., 2017), and so are methods to analyze these three-dimensional structures (Ascoli et al., 2009; Polavaram et al., 2014). However, the quantification of arbor-wide subcellular signals is not as common. Here we describe a protocol to reconstruct, analyze, and simulate multi-signal neural structures, starting from confocal image stacks. While we have employed this protocol to characterize cytoskeletal distributions in invertebrate sensory neurons, this system can suit any and all imaged signals across the neural arbor. Current multi-signal characterizations are often qualitative in nature. By adapting and using the multi-signal quantification protocol described below, researchers will be able to present their observations in a measurable way. This system will, in principle, allow the subcellular characterization of any neuronal property captured through multi-channel microscopic imaging, including concentrations and spatial distributions of various molecules in cytoplasm, ion channels, cellular organelles etc. Here, we specifically demonstrate single neuron reconstructions of larval fruit fly dendritic arborization (da) neurons followed by the quantification of microtubule and F-actin quantities. We begin from two-channel image stacks in the .czi file format, with the red channel representing microtubule and the green channel representing F-actin. The fly strain used for Class IV da neuron imaging is: w1118, UAS-GMA::GFP; GAL4[477],UAS-mCherry::Jupiter; the fly strain used for Class I da neuron imaging is: w1118, UAS-GMA::GFP; +; GAL4[221],UAS-mCherry::Jupiter. For overexpression of Formin3 (Form3) the following strain is used: UAS-form3-B1 (Tanaka et al., 2004). This protocol describes the process that begins after the confocal image generation.
